title: Small kindnesses
hook: a short surah condemns those who refuse even small kindnesses (Quran 107)
tomorrow: why does one verse switch from 'O ye who believe' to 'O mankind'?

segments.voice: Yesterday, which of the favors: a refrain that wants an answer, and the jinn who gave it every time. Which favor.

A knock at the door. The neighbor needs a pot for tonight's dinner, or a bucket, just for an hour. In one short surah of the Quran, that knock is the test. The surah opens on a man: "Hast thou observed him who belieth religion? That is he who repelleth the orphan, And urgeth not the feeding of the needy." Then it turns to people at prayer. Woe, it says, to worshippers who are heedless of their prayer, who want to be seen at worship, "Yet refuse small kindnesses!"
screen: `A KNOCK: CAN I BORROW A POT?` → `HE PUSHES THE ORPHAN AWAY.` → `SEEN AT PRAYER.` → `YET REFUSE SMALL KINDNESSES.`

segments.voice: That last word, al-ma'un, gives the surah its name, and it answers yesterday's question. Small kindnesses, but which ones? Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, one of the Prophet's companions, says in a report in Abu Dawud's collection: in the time of the Messenger, we counted al-ma'un as lending the bucket and the cooking pot. Here's why that's sharp. The people in the surah are praying. They're seen at worship. What's missing isn't prayer. It's the pot. The surah ties the two together: worship that won't lend a bucket next door has lost its point. And it doesn't stand alone. Two days ago, ad-Duha reminded the Prophet that he had been an orphan, and said: the orphan, don't oppress. Here, the very first picture is a man who pushes the orphan away. So, in this surah, prayer and small help to neighbors belong together, and the small help counts. Not grand charity. The bucket. And the detail that sticks: in one companion's memory, the word that names this surah meant the things you lend from your kitchen.
screen: `AL-MA'UN: THE SURAH'S NAME.` · `IBN MAS'UD: THE BUCKET AND THE POT.` · `PRAYING, YET REFUSING.` · `THE ORPHAN AGAIN.` · then, large: `SMALL KINDNESSES.`

segments.voice: Pick up your phone and bring to mind one neighbor, coworker or friend. Send one plain line offering something small you have that they might need: a ride, a charger, a dish, an hour. Keep it light, the size of a borrowed pot.

howItsDone: Surah al-Ma'un is a short surah from the Quran's last part; Muslim teachers use it to show that prayer and care for the orphan, the needy and the neighbor belong together.

chat.meaning: Ibn Mas'ud said al-ma'un meant lending the bucket and the cooking pot. The surah faults worshippers who refuse even a kindness that small.
